**Closing, possession, and occupancy (Paragraphs 5 and 6)**
Closing shall take place on or before August 29th, 2022 at a mutually agreed-upon location, with Seller paying all state and county transfer taxes and other costs required to convey clear title, and any extension of these time frames required to be in writing. Legal action related to the property's condition or the agreement must be brought within the shorter of the time provided by law or one year after Closing. The parties are advised to consult an attorney; no verbal agreements are enforceable and time is of the essence. Brookstone Realtors LLC, its brokers, offices, directors, employees, and agents are released from claims regarding property condition or performance. A final walk-through is permitted within 48 hours prior to closing. Under Paragraph 37, $595.00 will be collected from the Buyer at closing as a Broker Review and Compliance fee, a portion of which may be shared with the Designated Agent. 2022_22_09202022_policy_update_recommend.paragraph: Prepared for the Troy School District Board of Education meeting of September 20, 2022, this policy update recommendation walks section by section through the district's policy manual and proposes amendments in the 1000 Bylaws, 2000 Students, 3000 Curriculum and Instruction, 4000 Personnel, 5000 Business, and 8000 General Policies series, with no changes recommended for the 6000 Facilities and Operations series. The most consequential item is a comprehensive rewrite of the 3000 series covering curriculum development, parent and family engagement, textbook and instructional material selection, and media center materials, prompted by escalating public scrutiny of curriculum decisions and framed around MCL 380.1278 and MCL 380.1421/22.
2022_22_09202022_policy_update_recommend.page:
**Purpose**
A section-by-section set of recommended policy manual amendments presented to the Troy School District Board of Education on September 20, 2022.

**Bylaws - 1000 Series**
Policy 1000.01, Organization and Functioning of the Board: the sub-policy "Removal from Office" addresses removal of Board officers from officer positions rather than removal from the Board itself, so it should be retitled "Removal from Officer Positions" to eliminate ambiguity.

**Students - 2000 Series**
Policy 2000.01, Children of Non-Resident Employees: a loophole allowed a person to obtain employment, enroll a child, then voluntarily leave employment while the pupil kept enrollment without tuition. Revised language, consistent with the State Aid Act and Pupil Accounting Manual, permits tuition-free enrollment of a non-resident employee's child in the K-12 program, continuing through graduation or receipt of a certificate of completion so long as the employee remains employed, and also continuing where the employee no longer works for the district due to layoff or elimination of the position. "Employee" means an individual with regularly scheduled hours while school is in session and excludes seasonal, coaching, and third party contracted employees including substitute teachers; eligibility starts at the next school term or semester.

Policy 2000.06, Personal Electronic Devices: use is limited to scheduled lunch, before and after the regular school day, and teacher-directed educational purposes; otherwise devices must be powered off and out of sight in backpacks, purses, or lockers. New language bars broadcasting or recording audio, images, or video of any student, staff member, or other person without permission, excepting curricular and extracurricular activities such as athletic events and arts performances.

Policy 2000.07, Wellness: policy and administrative regulation 2000.07-AR are updated to match current federal regulatory guidance on student wellness and nutrition.

**Curriculum and Instruction - 3000 Series**
The entire section was reviewed in light of escalating attacks on schools and boards over curriculum. 3000.01 Curriculum Development is revised for Revised School Code compliance, citing MCL 380.1278 and requiring Board approval of core academic curriculum changes to the extent Michigan law requires. 3000.02 is renamed "Parent and Family Engagement (PFE)" with Title I obligations restated. 3000.03 Instruction drops an extraneous word, leaving "research based and peer reviewed instructional methodologies." 3000.04 is retitled "Textbooks, Technology, and Other Essential Curricular Materials" and wholly replaced, citing MCL 380.1421/22 and delegating approval and purchase of non-textbook instructional materials to the Superintendent. 3000.05 becomes "Selection of Media Center/Library Materials."

**Personnel - 4000 Series**
Under Policy 4000.03, the Alcohol and Drug Free Workplace sub-policy gains express authority for the Superintendent to require a medical examination on reasonable suspicion, and the Medical Examinations sub-policy adds that trigger to its list. Examination costs are borne by the School District, the employee signs a release, and the physician's report goes to the Superintendent and into a separate confidential personnel file.

**Business - 5000 Series**
New sub-policy "Real Property and Structures" under Policy 5000.03 (Purchasing) supplies acquisition authority to match existing disposition authority and expressly authorizes the Superintendent to execute closing documents. Policy 5000.05 (Surplus Property) renames "Land, Buildings, Facilities, and Real Estate" to "Real Property and Structures." Policy 5000.11 (Online Fundraising) deletes the list of sites naming DonorsChoose.org, Kickstarter.com, GoFundMe.com, and CrowdRise.com.

**General Policies - 8000 Series**
Policy 8000.07 and regulation 8000.07-AR are revised to separate Title IX matters from other discrimination and harassment matters, following the 2020 U.S. Department of Education guidelines that updated the regulations for the first time since 1997. Draft Title IX regulations issued in June 2022 are not final and are not integrated, with finalization not expected until approximately late 2023. The policy prohibits discrimination on the basis of race, color, national origin, religion, sex including sexual orientation and gender identity, marital status, genetic information, disability, age, or any other basis prohibited by law, and designates the Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services and Title IX Coordinator to supervise implementation.
2022_22_09202022_policy_update_recommend.verbose:
**Document and setting**
A recommended policy update memorandum prepared for the Troy School District Board of Education meeting of September 20, 2022, organized by policy manual series and stating for each proposed change the reason and the recommended language.

**Bylaws - 1000 Series**
Policy 1000.01, Organization and Functioning of the Board: Removal from Office. The policy addresses removal of Board officers from their Board officer positions, not removal from the Board itself, so the sub-policy heading should become "Removal from Officer Positions" to eliminate ambiguity.

**Students - 2000 Series**
Policy 2000.01, Admission and Enrollment: Children of Non-Resident Employees. Consistent with specific language in the State Aid Act and the Pupil Accounting Manual, the memo recommends updating the sub-policy after discovery of a small loophole in which a person could obtain employment, have their child enrolled under the sub-policy, then voluntarily leave employment while the pupil maintained enrollment without paying tuition. Recommended language: a child of a non-resident employee may enroll without tuition provided the student is enrolling in the K-12 program; once enrolled the student may continue through graduation or receipt of a certificate of completion as long as the employee remains employed with the School District, and may also continue if the employee no longer works for the District due to layoff or elimination of the position. The policy does not bar long-term suspension or expulsion for a violation of the Student Code of Conduct. An "employee" is an individual with regularly scheduled hours while school is in session, excluding seasonal, coaching, and third party contracted employees including substitute teachers, and becomes eligible at the start of the next school term or semester.

Policy 2000.06, Behavior: Personal Electronic Devices. Responding to client interest in language barring students from using cell phones or similar devices to record or photograph others at school without permission, subject to common sense exceptions such as a sporting event or arts performance, the memo adds underlined text to the sub-policy identified as "Distribution and Posting of Materials." The District reserves the right to prohibit possession or use of personal electronic devices on School District property or at School District-related functions; a "personal electronic device" is a privately owned device used for audio, video, or text communications; use is permitted only during the student's scheduled lunch time, before and after the regular school day, and as directed by a teacher or other professional staff member for educational purposes; devices must otherwise be powered off and out of sight in backpacks, purses, or lockers; broadcasting or recording audio, images, or video of any student, staff member, or other person without that person's permission is barred, excepting curricular or extracurricular activities for which personal recording is generally permitted; and the Superintendent may develop regulations.

Policy 2000.07, Health and Safety: Wellness. Citing significantly increased federal agency attention to student wellness and nutrition, changes to the policy and to administrative regulation 2000.07-AR bring the district into compliance with the latest regulatory guidance and interpretations. The Board recognizes student wellness as integral to learning, growth, and development; the District will promote proper nutrition, nutrition education, and regular physical activity; the Board has adopted a Wellness Policy as required by law, periodically reviewed; and the Superintendent will develop administrative regulations.

**Curriculum and Instruction - 3000 Series**
Given the current political environment and escalating attacks on schools and boards over curriculum development, approval, and associated choices, the team reviewed and revised the entire 3000 section.

Policy 3000.01, Curriculum Development. Revised for compliance with the Revised School Code and to clarify the board's responsibilities under Michigan law. The Board directs the Superintendent to develop, implement, and evaluate the core academic curriculum, which must be consistent with the Board's policy on Student Learning and Achievement, meet or exceed all State of Michigan requirements for instructional programs, and be standards based and founded on legally-compliant, research based grade level learning and achievement standards leading to a School District diploma. It must also cover career and technical education students and address students of all abilities, students with disabilities, and gifted students. Changes to the core academic curriculum must be approved by the Board to the extent required by Michigan law, citing MCL 380.1278.

Policy 3000.02, Parental Involvement, renamed "Parent and Family Engagement (PFE)." The Superintendent will develop regulations in consultation with parents and families covering cooperation to develop students' intellectual and vocational skills in a safe and positive environment, review of curriculum, textbooks, and teaching materials, observation of instructional activities other than testing and assessments, and disclosure or use of student information for sales or marketing. Under Title I the District informs parents and families of the program and its objectives, trains them and Title I staff, consults regularly, involves them in program design, operation, and evaluation, and provides for full participation of those who lack literacy skills or whose native language is not English. Services funded with state and local money in Title I schools must be comparable to those in non-Title I schools.

Policy 3000.03, Instruction, written in one line of the memo as Policy 3003.03. An extraneous word is removed, leaving that to the maximum extent feasible instruction will be delivered using research based and peer reviewed instructional methodologies.

Policy 3000.04, retitled Textbooks, Technology, and Other Essential Curricular Materials. Because the former Textbooks and Other Instructional Materials policy has become the focus of many community groups, the language is comprehensively updated and wholly replaced. Textbooks or their modern equivalent are fundamental to delivery of the core academic curriculum, and the Superintendent may use well-qualified administrators and teachers to assist in selecting textbooks recommended to the Board for approval to the extent required by Michigan law, citing MCL 380.1421/22. Other instructional materials do not require Board approval; the Board delegates authority to approve and purchase them to the Superintendent, and they must be compatible with the Board-approved core academic curriculum.

Policy 3000.05, retitled "Selection of Media Center/Library Materials." Amid increasing scrutiny from community members, the Board intends students be provided access to a wide variety of educational materials in various media, with the Superintendent authorized to make or approve purchases for the media center and classroom libraries and to receive recommendations from professional staff members, parents, and students.

**Personnel - 4000 Series**
Policy 4000.03, Conditions of Employment: Alcohol and Drug Free Workplace. Though the district's authority to send a suspected employee for a medical examination was never legally in doubt, clients asked for explicit language. The Board maintains a workplace free of alcohol and illegal drugs and of prescription drugs for which the employee lacks a current valid prescription; an employee or volunteer who manufactures, distributes, dispenses, possesses, or uses alcohol or any drug in the workplace, or is present in the workplace under the influence, is subject to discipline up to and including discharge; and the Superintendent may require a medical examination on reasonable suspicion that the employee is under the influence of drugs, alcohol, or illegal substances while performing job duties or on school grounds.

Policy 4000.03, Conditions of Employment: Medical Examinations. The Superintendent or designee may require an examination when required or permitted by federal or state law or by the employee's contract of employment; when information suggests a health condition may be negatively affecting the employee's ability to perform essential job functions with or without accommodations, or that the employee is a direct threat to their own or others' safety; when medical documentation for a health leave remains insufficient after an opportunity to supplement; or on reasonable suspicion of being under the influence. All costs are borne by the School District, the employee signs a release authorizing the physician to report directly to the Superintendent, and a copy is kept in a separate confidential personnel file.

**Business - 5000 Series**
Policy 5000.03, Purchasing: Real Property and Structures, a new sub-policy. Baseline policies referenced disposition of land, buildings, facilities, and real estate but never expressly provided matching acquisition authority, and title agencies routinely require a board resolution plus a document granting an individual, most commonly the Board President or Superintendent, authority to execute closing documents. Under the new language the Superintendent may identify real property and structures suitable for purchase and recommend procedures to the Board; Board approval is required for both the process and the ultimate purchase or acquisition; and the Superintendent is authorized to execute any and all closing documents. It is separate and distinct from Policy 5000.05.

Policy 5000.05, Surplus Property. The sub-policy "Land, Buildings, Facilities, and Real Estate" is renamed "Real Property and Structures," with the original terms struck. The Superintendent may identify property no longer required for School District purposes and recommend procedures to the Board; Board approval is required for the process and the ultimate sale or disposition; and the Superintendent may execute closing documents.

Policy 5000.11, Online Fundraising. The list of potential fundraising sites naming DonorsChoose.org, Kickstarter.com, GoFundMe.com, and CrowdRise.com is deleted as superfluous. The retained language bars employees from creating, posting, or sponsoring an online fundraiser seeking public funds for school purposes or using the District's name, logo, or likeness without prior written consent from the Superintendent, and makes property so secured District property rather than the employee's.

**Facilities and Operations - 6000 Series and School and Community Relations - 7000 Series**
No recommended updates are listed for the 6000 series, and the 7000 series heading appears with no recommendations under it.

**General Policies - 8000 Series**
Policy 8000.07, Discrimination and Harassment. No topic has garnered as much attention in the past few years as Title IX; in 2020 the U.S. Department of Education issued new guidelines for implementation and enforcement, updating the regulations for the first time since 1997, and 2021-22 was the first meaningful opportunity for most districts to live with them during a normal school year, a road that was at times bumpy. Revisions to policy and administrative regulation 8000.07 and 8000.07-AR provide operational clarity while drawing a clear distinction between Title IX issues and other matters of discrimination and harassment. New draft Title IX regulations issued by the U.S. Department of Education in June 2022 are not yet final and are not integrated into these updates, with finalization not expected until approximately late 2023. The policy commits the Board to a learning and working environment in which all individuals are treated with dignity and respect, free from illegal discrimination and harassment based on a legally prohibited characteristic, with no tolerance for discrimination or harassment on the basis of race, color, national origin, religion, sex including sexual orientation and gender identity, marital status, genetic information, disability, age, or any other basis prohibited by law, and designates the Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services and Title IX Coordinator to supervise implementation of the policy and its implementing regulations.
